Case_19007/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Figure 1: Photograph of the raised papular rash on the posterior scalp

description.short_caption: Photograph of erythematous papular rash on the posterior scalp.
description.detailed_description: This image shows the posterior scalp of a bald individual with numerous erythematous papules distributed across the skin. The lesions are irregularly spaced and vary slightly in size, with some areas appearing more confluent. The surrounding skin shows mild erythema without overt signs of ulceration or crusting. The image is well-lit, allowing clear visualization of the rash morphology.

Case_19007/figure2.jpg.source_caption: Figure 2: Photograph of petechial rash on upper thighs

description.short_caption: Photograph showing petechial rash on the upper thighs.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph depicts the anterior aspect of both upper thighs. Numerous small, non-blanching, red to purple macules are scattered across the skin, consistent with a petechial rash. The lesions vary slightly in size and are distributed irregularly. The surrounding skin appears otherwise normal without significant erythema or swelling. The image is well-lit, and the findings are clearly visible.
visible_findings: numerous small, non-blanching red to purple macules

Case_19007/figure6.jpg.source_caption: Figure 6: Parvovirus immunohistochemistry positive on bone marrow biopsy

description.short_caption: Parvovirus immunohistochemistry positive on bone marrow biopsy.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a bone marrow biopsy stained with immunohistochemistry. A single large cell with a prominent, dark brown-stained intranuclear inclusion is visible, consistent with parvovirus infection. Surrounding cells are stained blue, likely representing hematopoietic cells counterstained with hematoxylin. The brown staining indicates the presence of parvoviral antigen within the nucleus.
visible_findings: dark brown intranuclear inclusion in a single large cell

Case_19007/figure5.jpg.source_caption: Figure 5: Trephine hematoxylin and eosin staining showing parvovirus inclusion body

description.short_caption: Bone marrow trephine biopsy with H&E stain showing parvovirus inclusion body.
description.detailed_description: This histopathology image shows a bone marrow trephine biopsy stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). A prominent intranuclear inclusion body, characteristic of parvovirus infection, is visible within a hematopoietic precursor cell. The inclusion appears as a dense, eosinophilic structure surrounded by a clear halo, highlighted by the black arrow. The surrounding marrow shows normal cellular elements with no significant architectural disruption.
visible_findings: intranuclear inclusion body with eosinophilic staining
normal marrow cellular elements in the background

Case_19007/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Figure 4: Wright-Giemsa stain of bone marrow aspirate showing large parvovirus B19 erythroblast

description.short_caption: Wright-Giemsa stain of bone marrow aspirate showing a large erythroblast with viral inclusions.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Wright-Giemsa stained bone marrow aspirate. A large erythroblast is prominently visible in the center, stained blue with a dense nucleus. The cytoplasm appears basophilic, and there are visible inclusions consistent with viral infection. Surrounding cells include smaller erythroid precursors and other hematopoietic cells. The arrow highlights the erythroblast of interest.

Case_19007/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Figure 3: Photographs of the right ankle showing swelling and petechiae

description.short_caption: Photograph of the right lower leg showing swelling, petechiae, and discoloration.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows the right lower leg and ankle with significant swelling, extensive petechiae, and areas of reddish-purple discoloration. The findings are most prominent over the anterior and lateral aspects of the leg. The skin appears tense, and there is evidence of possible subcutaneous edema. No open wounds or ulcerations are visible in this image.
visible_findings: swelling of the right lower leg and ankle
